messages:
maria: Heads up — since the rack swap in us-west2 we’ve seen a burst of tiny-gang migrations and ~150 GPU preempts in the last 30m. Anyone else seeing reshard-induced churn?

sam: yep noticed it around 11:12 UTC. pods moving between nodes in the same AZ, then slow kubelet readiness and kube-proxy flapping.

noah: logs show mix of latebind + affinity scoring oscillation. scheduler score jump when node labels updated after the rack repair.

lee: can you paste the scheduler debug snapshot? maybe the new node annotation is causing a tie-breaker flip.

maria: paste:```
I0311 11:12:18.123456 1 scheduler_pred.go:234] scoring: pod=trainer-xyz node=gpu-022 score=6.5
I0311 11:12:18.123457 1 scheduler_pred.go:234] scoring: pod=trainer-xyz node=gpu-053 score=6.7
I0311 11:12:18.123458 1 scheduler_pred.go:234] scoring: pod=trainer-xyz node=gpu-022 score=6.3
```

anita: that looks like nondeterministic tie-breaker when topologySpread + custom affinity present. Also saw NVLINK buddy changes after firmware update on that rack.

sam: infra metrics: NIC TX on rack B spiked ~50% during migrations, might be saturating interconnect and slowing pod readiness.

infra-oncall: triggered incident runbook: running descheduler to evacuate tiny-gang fragments and then re-compact. Will coordinate canary.

ops-bot: descheduler-bot scheduled descheduler job: run_id=ds-20260311-3 window=5m policy=RemoveDuplicates+LowNodeUtilization

noah: please hold traffic for the affected model routes if possible — the canary fallback isn't yet enabled for that deployment.

maria: quick mitigation idea: add a temporary soft-taint on nodes in the repaired rack to prevent new latebind placements for 10m, let existing pods settle, then drain selectively. Thoughts?

lee: soft-taint SGTM. Use taint:node.k8s.redwood/reshard-hold:NoSchedule:NoExecute (duration 10m) and annotate the nodes so rollout tools ignore them.

anita: also reduce scheduler preemption aggressiveness: set --min-replicas-for-preemption=2 on the scheduler flags for that AZ for the short term. That should reduce ripple evictions.

infra-oncall: applying soft-taint to nodes gpu-050..gpu-058 now. ops-bot:```
kubectl taint nodes gpu-050 gpu-051 gpu-052 gpu-053 gpu-054 gpu-055 gpu-056 gpu-057 gpu-058 reshard-hold=true:NoSchedule --overwrite
```

ops-bot: taints applied.

maria: observed a drop in new placements after taint. But we still see a handful of pending tiny pods stuck in Queue — maybe need to bump warm-pool for the AZ.

sam: warming extra 4 slots from warm-pool for us-west2c for 20m. ops-bot:```
kubectl scale deployment/gpu-warmpool-usw2c --replicas=4 -n infra
```

ops-bot: warmpool scaled.

noah: FYI this will increase short-term cost ~0.6 GPU-hours but saves ~120 preempt cycles which were spiking. worth it.

anita: after the descheduler run completes, we should run a targeted placement simulation to catch scoring oscillations. I'll open a quick perf-eval PR with the failing pod, scheduler flags, and topology labels.

lee: also add a cheap check in the rollout tool: if node annotation change within last 15m, avoid mass rebinds — simple debounce.

infra-oncall: descheduler finished. removed 98 duplicate tiny pods, re-packed 63 pods onto 12 nodes.

maria: traffic restored to canary. early latency metrics look OK. will monitor for 2h and then remove soft-taint.

ops-bot: reminder to remove soft-taint at 13:00 UTC:```
kubectl taint nodes gpu-050 gpu-051 gpu-052 gpu-053 gpu-054 gpu-055 gpu-056 gpu-057 gpu-058 reshard-hold:NoSchedule- --overwrite
```

noah: follow-up: we should add a heuristic to the scheduler to penalize nodes with recent firmware/annotation churn for 10m. I'll draft the change.

anita: agree — also log NVLINK topology changes into infra-events so we can correlate automatically next time.

maria: thanks all. summary: applied short soft-taint + warmpool bump + descheduler run; preempts down; monitoring continued. filing brief post-incident note.
